scope.purpose: Bounded Feature C extraction priority; not a combat ontology or clear predictor.

authority.source_resolution: Each boss source_ref is its manifest canonical_id. The manifest resolves the checksum-pinned bounded capture; parsed_section_sha256 identifies the interpreted section. Feasibility fixtures cannot add mechanics.
precedence: general mechanics corpus and capability taxonomy

classification_contract.required: Boss evidence states a hard affinity, action-count, timing, counter, immunity, or equivalent gate; absence invalidates that modeled plan.
classification_contract.high_value: Evidence-backed counter materially improves modeled viability but alternatives may exist; it affects extraction priority and later ranking, never hard legality by itself.
classification_contract.contextual: Evidence-backed advantage or caveat that may differentiate a plan but is neither mandatory nor a Feature C extraction driver by itself.
classification_contract.unresolved: The bounded source is unknown, incomplete, stochastic, or outside the current taxonomy; no requirement or capability credit may be inferred.
classification_contract.unknown_policy: Unknown affinity or mechanic detail remains unresolved. Missing, rejected, untagged, and ambiguous character evidence remains distinct from explicitly proven absence.

affinity_safe_damage.feature_c_action: Expand and prove primary-damage element/type extraction across all canonical identities.

multi_mode_damage.feature_c_action: Propose source-backed element/type qualifiers; do not infer team coverage from a generic damage tag.

burst_deadline.feature_c_action: Extract the component capabilities; keep exact turn and damage simulation out of scope.

hit_action_threshold.feature_c_action: Preserve explicit hit/action evidence and do not treat barrier pierce as equivalent without boss proof.

multi_entity_damage.feature_c_action: Capture proven target scope separately from generic direct damage.

trigger_avoidance.feature_c_action: Keep negative boss constraints explicit; never manufacture a positive character capability from them.

offensive_stat_suppression.feature_c_action: Prioritize enemy-directed PWR/INT reduction with reviewed direction and target.

hp_sustain.feature_c_action: Prioritize healing and survival proof without simulating exact survival.

mp_sustain.feature_c_action: Prioritize party MP recovery for drain and endurance encounters.

status_counterplay.feature_c_action: Prioritize party cleanse/immunity; do not confuse boss-inflicted Pain/Poison with player setup.

zone_counterplay.feature_c_action: Extract deploy/awaken evidence and queue explicit zone-removal/replacement facts; preserve no-zone constraints.

enemy_buff_control.feature_c_action: Admit an atomic dispel proposal only from explicit source text; Buff Reversal is not dispel.

reset_resilience.feature_c_action: Retain duration, trigger, and limited-use evidence so later ranking can prefer re-applicable support.

resistance_break.feature_c_action: Prioritize enemy-directed resistance and weakness manipulation with exact scope.

turn_order_control.feature_c_action: Extract speed effects; retain explicit timing text without claiming exact sequencing.

fixed_damage_response.feature_c_action: Treat as a survivability signal only; ordinary mitigation is not assumed to reduce fixed damage.

debuff_cleanse.feature_c_action: Prioritize party debuff removal separately from status-ailment cleanse.

af_support.feature_c_action: Keep contextual because several bosses disable, reset, reduce, or taboo AF.

pain_poison_setup.feature_c_action: Retain as a strategic breadth floor; the boss corpus does not make player-applied Pain/Poison a hard counter.

boss_matrix.evidence_summary: Four elemental resistances and summoned companions.
Random non-type magic pressure; all affinity dimensions are unknown.
Multiple attack modes are explicitly required; status and blow-away pressure recur.
Confusion and large fixed or percent-HP attacks; affinity is unknown.
All attack types resist before a brief all-weakness window; AF is unavailable early.
Mixed damage, random ailments, and boss physical/type resistance buffs; affinity is unknown.
AF is unavailable; physical/magic phases, fixed damage, ailments, and full resets recur.
Fire weakness, broad resistances, delayed targeting, ailments, and HP-halving pressure.
Two-stage add encounter with core immunity, multiple damage modes, dispels, drains, and a wipe clock.
Explicit 15-hit then 30-hit barriers plus ailments and MP-percent pressure.
Pain, Poison, sleep, stat debuffs, weapon resistances, and an AF stopper.
Element-triggered self changes, reserve knockback, MP drain, stun, healing, and reset behavior.
Mixed affinity, poison, position marks and petrification, speed buffs, and fixed damage.
Boss resistance buffs, party stat debuffs, max-HP pressure, resets, Pain, and fixed damage; affinity is unknown.
Random element/zone state and lethal matching-element counters, plus resistance, confusion, priority stun, and an AF stopper.
Six-element resistance, repeated percent/fixed damage, ailments, forced reserve, resets, and AF stopper.
Up to five minions, MP and stat pressure, stun, physical resistance, and boss-debuff resets.
Earth actions create ten-hit shields; stoppers add minions/zones amid displacement, ailments, resets, and fixed damage.
Paired multi-phase enemies apply ailments, zones, debuffs, MP damage, priority healing, and resets; affinity is unknown.
Earth weakness, physical resistance, ailments, revive/reset/zone transition, and a one-turn skill gauge.
Shade weakness, physical resistance, ailments, revive/reset/zone transition, and a one-turn skill gauge.
Thirteen revivals and escalating resistance culminate in an unavoidable next-turn kill; affinity is unknown.
Attack-type-dependent resistance/barrier changes, high fixed damage, stun, and stopper attacks; affinity fields are unknown.
Crystal is the sole safe elemental plan; non-Crystal attacks are countered, while adds deploy zones and resistance buffs.
Two entities have conflicting weakness, resistance, null, and absorb profiles; speed and ailments add pressure.
All attack types resist, a 15-turn unlock condition applies, and a minion imposes changing AF/heal/element/cleanse/zone taboos.
Magic damage powers the boss aura; AF/zone reset, repeated zone deployment, ailments, resets, revival, and evasion recur.
Physical damage powers an aura and later becomes null; the boss resets AF/zones, inflicts confusion, heals, and applies fixed damage.
Twenty-five action-consumed resistance stacks, attack counters, fixed damage, zone breaks, and low-PWR/INT punishment define a long fight.
Water is the only non-null or non-resistant listed offense; the bounded section proves 90% physical resistance but not the advertised full rotation.

priority_summary.basis: Every modeled plan needs neutral-or-better usable primary damage; the baseline proves this for only 10 identities.
Ailments recur across all cohorts and status-counter proof is sparse.
Seven bosses explicitly require or force a damage-mode change; generic direct_damage does not prove the needed element/type breadth.
Seven bosses punish an element, attack type, zone, stat-debuff threshold, or other action; negative constraints must stay explicit.
High incoming damage is recurrent while proven mitigation covers 16 identities.
Fourteen bosses clear buffs, debuffs, zones, or related setup; reusable support needs duration/trigger proof.
Fixed or percent-HP pressure recurs, but it cannot be reduced to generic mitigation or exact survival simulation.
Resistance pressure spans 18 bosses when ranking-only context is included; the baseline offensive-enablement family covers 21 identities.
Ten bosses visibly buff or stack defenses/offense; the current taxonomy has Buff Reversal but no atomic enemy dispel.
Speed, priority, preemption, and delayed actions recur, but exact sequencing remains outside scope.
Thirteen bosses support sustain as a ranking factor and baseline recovery proof covers seven identities.
Nine bosses deploy, destroy, reset, punish, or otherwise interact with zones; current proof covers 12 identities.
Seven encounters use companions, minions, or paired enemies, and target scope is not proven by generic damage.
Seven bosses create MP or endurance pressure; baseline recovery is sparse.
Seven encounters contain explicit windows, clocks, gauges, or next-turn failure pressure; extract component offense without simulating damage.
Three bosses explicitly consume hits or ally actions; barrier_pierce is not assumed equivalent.
Five bosses impose sustained stat or resistance reductions; remove_debuff stays distinct from status cleanse.
Two bosses provide direct corpus support, while reviewed direction and target remain essential to avoid treating self buffs as enemy suppression.
Five bosses force or advertise reserve displacement; knockback immunity is an exact atomic counter.
AF can help action/burst plans, but multiple bosses disable, reset, reduce, or taboo it; retain breadth without treating it as universal.
The corpus frequently shows boss-inflicted ailments but no hard need for player-applied Pain/Poison; retain the approved low strategic-breadth floor without conflating directions.

feature_c_priority_bands.instruction: Attempt deterministic full-catalog extraction first. Add only source-provable atomic capabilities or qualifiers; explicit gaps stay non-authoritative until the normal taxonomy/review path admits them.
Extract after P0 or alongside it when the same source fact proves both. Preserve timing, target, duration, trigger, and availability rather than synthesizing combat outcomes.
Retain as approved strategic-breadth dimensions. They are not boss-mandatory, and boss-inflicted Pain/Poison never proves player-applied setup.

threshold_contract.reason: The corpus materially ranks extraction families but does not establish a defensible alternate identity-count floor. AF and Pain/Poison remain contextual breadth dimensions, so their deliberately low floors are retained rather than silently relaxed.

keep: milestone completion evidence and threshold decision
purge_or_ignore: generated review queues until Feature C owns them
